title: Crimson Skies - High Road to Revenge (USA) (En,Fr,De,Zh,Ko).xiso.iso
queue_order: A1 B1 A2 B2, each a separate request.sh --title soak, --device thor, --route crimson-skies, --seconds 240, --expect this file
prediction: #427, lever 4 of docs/investigations/perf-architecture.md: native ELF TLS (minSdk 29), inline LSE atomics (-march=armv8.2-a) and no intra-library PLT (-Wl,-Bsymbolic). The lever's size is a BOUND, not a measured gain: in the dated 09-11 Crimson simpleperf capture, 4.40% of vCPU-thread samples and 3.73% of PFIFO-thread samples were in emutls, outline atomics, PLT stubs and pthread TLS. Removing all of it saves at most that share of vCPU time; Crimson is vCPU-bound (busy 41.5 of a 50.2 ms frame), so frame time can fall by at most ~4.4% and gfps can rise by at most ~4.6%. Crimson's run-to-run spread on the Thor is of that order (titleplay p1: 110-240 s median 26, range 14-29, gfps capped at 30), so this A/B may not resolve the gain. That outcome is reported as BELOW RESOLUTION, with the bound as the lever's size.

legs.M0 (instrument): Every run has >= 30 hakuX-perf lines between 110 and 240 s and its route reached 'mark gameplay'. A run without them is VOID, not zero, and is rerun once.
legs.F0 (falsifier, the counter in the binary: symcheck.py on the dispatcher-built APKs. A: emutls_calls >= 1000, outline_calls >= 1000, plt_internal >= 5000 (local build of master aaf01a1cef: 1828, 1599, 8753). B: tls_segment true, plt_internal == 0, emutls_calls <= 10 and outline_calls <= 400 with every remaining caller in the NDK's prebuilt libc++ (std::__ndk1 locale setup, __cxxabiv1 thread_atexit); local build of b_ref: 6, 289, 0. FAILS in the world where the dispatcher's build does not carry the flags (a cached CMake configure, or an ANDROID_PLATFORM that does not follow minSdk). Then no soak reading is attributable, and the lever is reported INERT HERE until the binary is right.
legs.F1 (falsifier, the counter in the profil: A 30 s simpleperf cpu-clock capture of Crimson gameplay on each APK, vCPU thread, counted per sample with docs/lanes/perfarch/profile_categories.py. A: samples in __emutls_get_address + __aarch64_{cas,swp,ld*} + pthread_getspecific >= 1.0% of vCPU samples. B: samples in __emutls_get_address + __aarch64_* == 0 on the vCPU thread. PLT-stub samples inside libxemu.so in B <= 50% of A's (the 635 PLT entries left in B call other libraries; the split of the 1.08% between internal and external targets is not known, so 50% is a guess and is labelled as one). FAILS if B still samples the helpers: then something on the vCPU path is not built with these flags.
legs.P1 (fps, the number that counts): median over runs of each run's median gfps in 110-240 s: B / A within [0.98, 1.08]. Below 0.98 FAILS as a regression. Above 1.08 FAILS: the change exceeds the bound, so something besides these three mechanisms moved and the gain is not attributable to them.
legs.P2 (resolution): If |B - A| (median gfps) is not larger than the larger within-arm difference (|A1 - A2|, |B1 - B2|), the A/B is BELOW RESOLUTION. P1 is then read only as 'no regression', and the reported gain is the F1 bound, not a measured fps change.

must_not_move: pgraph: docs/testing/predictions/buildflags427-pgraph-inert.json (12 suites, identical captures, same refs)
no crash, no tombstone in logcat -b crash on any B run; gfps lines still printed at 240 s
expect_note: EMPTY ON PURPOSE: a soak writes no captures, so there is no golden key for ab_compare to judge. The legs are read off the gfps lines, symcheck.py and the host's simpleperf captures; the content hash recorded at queue time is what makes a widened leg detectable.
